chunks: As for what al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammam ibn Isa and Khalaf ibn Rabi', from al-Fudayl, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a female slave whom he had sexual relations with, and she died, and then he marries her daughter. He said: There is no harm; she is not in the same position as a free woman.
This report does not mention the sexual relation (in the prohibition), but rather it implies that he may marry her, and it is permissible for him to marry her later by owning her and using her.

And what is prohibited for him is the sexual relation with her, according to what was stated previously regarding others, and that which also indicates that the ruling of the slave woman and the free woman in this matter is the same.

key_terms.يَطَؤُهَا: He has sexual relations with her

ai.seo_question: Does a man who has sexual relations with a female slave face the same prohibition on marrying her daughter as he would with a free woman?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi cites this report from Al-Saffar to clarify that the prohibition of marrying a daughter after cohabiting with her mother applies strictly to free women, whereas for female slaves, the owner may marry the daughter provided she is also owned. This distinction highlights the flexibility of ownership rights in Shia jurisprudence, where the act of 'wating' (cohabitation) does not create the same permanent marital bond prohibition as it does for free women. The text further notes that the ruling for the slave and free woman is considered equal in this specific context of ownership.
